title: Historic city 90 minutes from Newcastle named the most haunted in Europe
excerpt: Creepy history is set to be discovered just a short train journey from Newcastle
content:
In the approach to Halloween, everyone loves spooky stories and a new study has identified a top 10 list of Europe-wide locations that host some of the best - or worst - of them. And it has revealed Europe's most haunted city which, in news set to send shivers down the spine, turns out to lie less than 90 minutes by train from Newcastle.

Edinburgh, which as previously reported is already home to a pub which has been ranked among the most haunted in the UK, now sees its creepy reputation spread even further as it features top of a newly-revealed 'European Hauntability Index'. It was drawn up by travel company Iglu Cruise in response to people's searches for 'Halloween travel' - said to have surged in the UK by a record 85% this year.

It assessed 40 major destinations to draw up a list of top spooky getaways, looking at the likes of supply and demand of ghost tours; historic architecture - such as the number of historic crypts, cemeteries, catacombs, crypts, castles and ruins - and visitor reviews. Halloween night sunset times were also taken into consideration, to find out when the cloak of darkness would fall, adding another layer of spookiness.

And top of all came Edinburgh. The company's write-up of the Scottish capital says: "Edinburgh is well known for its historic architecture, underground vaults and ancient burial grounds." It reveals that the city's top spot in the index is mainly thanks to high tourist demand, with the city receiving almost 17,000 reviews for ghost tours.

On the night of Halloween, it says the sun will set there early, just after 4.30pm, "creating ideal conditions for evening walking tours through the Old Town". And, referencing the city's famous ancient graveyard and its underground 17th Century labyrinth of old homes, it adds: "Key attractions that drive interest include Greyfriars Kirkyard and the underground passages of the Real Mary King's Close."

The company says: "Edinburgh has taken the overall crown as Europe's most haunted city, closely followed by London and Rome." And considering the likes of the capital's Whitechapel history and the Italian capital's catacombs and crypt, that's quite a chilling label.

York, itself just about an hour by train from Newcastle and whose spooky stories include a famous ghostly sighting at its Treasurer's House, made it into the list too. It is ranked number five, just behind the Czech Republic capital of Prague in fourth place.

The rest of the top 10 list features other capital cities of Vienna in Austria; Budapest in Hungary; Stockholm in Sweden and Lisbon in Portugal while in 10th place is Brașov in Romana, its ranking apparently helped by fascination with Dracula folklore. Edinburgh has plenty dark folklore of its own while one ghost story - which gave rise to last year's ranking among 'the UK's most-haunted pubs' - is actually based upon a macabre true life story.

The White Hart Inn is a historic tavern in the busy heart of Edinburgh and its site at Grassmarket has links to the city's infamous one-time residents William Burke and William Hare. The murderers, who in the 1800s stalked its streets by night, made a lucrative living by killing people and selling their fresh corpses to medics to dissect for anatomical study.

When eventually caught, Hare gave evidence against Burke in turn for immunity from prosecution and a public execution saw his partner in crime hanged on a spot outside The White Hart Inn which, founded in 1516, is said to be home to a number of ghostly sightings.
